verticalInfoCards.title: Rituals and Aarti
verticalInfoCards.note: Similar to Nageshwar, male devotees are permitted to enter the main sanctum bare-chested to perform Abhishek on the lingam.

quote.text: “After marveling at the rock-cut Kailasa temple at Ellora, visiting Grishneshwar feels like seeing the living form of the same divine energy.”
quote.author: — An Art Historian

verticalInfoCards.description: The temple is an important pilgrimage site, often visited along with the Ellora and Ajanta Caves.

overview.title: Overview
overview.text: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga, located near the renowned Ellora Caves, is the last of the 12 sacred Jyotirlingas mentioned in the Shiva Purana. The temple is a beautiful example of Maratha architecture and holds deep spiritual significance as the culminating point of the Jyotirlinga pilgrimage.

mythology.title: Mythological Origin
mythology.text: The temple's origin is linked to a devout woman named Kusuma. She would create and immerse a Shiva lingam daily in a tank as part of her worship. Her husband's first wife, jealous of her piety, killed Kusuma's son. Grief-stricken but with unshaken faith, Kusuma continued her ritual. Pleased by her devotion, Lord Shiva resurrected her son and manifested himself as the Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga at that spot.

architecture.title: Architectural Highlights
points: The current temple was rebuilt in the 18th century by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore, a great patron of Hindu temples.
It is constructed from red rock and features a five-tiered shikhara (spire).
The temple walls are adorned with intricate carvings of various gods and goddesses.
The main hall is supported by 24 beautifully carved pillars, depicting scenes from Hindu mythology.
It is one of the smallest Jyotirlinga temples in terms of area.

significance.title: Spiritual Significance
points: It is revered as the 12th and final Jyotirlinga, marking the completion of the pilgrimage.
A visit to Grishneshwar is believed to bestow the benefits of visiting all 12 Jyotirlingas.
The temple's legend highlights the power of selfless devotion (bhakti) and divine compassion.
Its proximity to the Ellora Caves, especially the Kailasa Temple (Cave 16), creates a powerful spiritual circuit.

events.event: The temple was destroyed during the Delhi Sultanate period.
Rebuilt by Maloji Bhosale of Verul, grandfather of Shivaji.
The current structure was rebuilt by Ahilyabai Holkar after being destroyed again.

items.text: A darshan at Grishneshwar is believed to fulfill all desires and remove obstacles from life.
The water from the temple tank is considered holy and purifying.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga is a serene and beautiful temple that stands as a symbol of pure devotion and divine grace. Its location near the artistic marvels of Ellora makes it a perfect conclusion to a journey that combines history, art, and profound spirituality.

aboutPostCards.title: Major Festivals
items: Maha Shivratri – The main festival, celebrated with a grand fair and night-long prayers.
Shravan Maas – The holy month sees a large influx of devotees for special pujas.

aboutPostCards.title: Nearby Attractions
items: Ellora Caves – A UNESCO World Heritage site with monumental rock-cut caves.
Daulatabad Fort – A magnificent and historic fort.
Ajanta Caves – Another UNESCO World Heritage site, famous for its ancient murals.
Bibi Ka Maqbara – A beautiful mausoleum often called the 'Taj of the Deccan'.

methods.title: By Road
methods.description: Grishneshwar is well-connected by road to Aurangabad (30 km). Regular buses and taxis are available.

methods.title: Nearest Railway
methods.description: Aurangabad Railway Station (AWB) is the nearest major railhead.

methods.title: Nearest Airport
methods.description: Aurangabad Airport (IXU) is the closest, approximately 37 km away.

mapSection.title: Temple Location
mapSection.description: Located in the village of Verul, less than a kilometer from the Ellora Caves, near Aurangabad in Maharashtra.
